name: Paired Root Extensions Are Intrinsically Recoverable from Their Sections
statement: Let an ample family have a marked degree-two corner root. Translate the root to zero and recover its three nontrivial sections $A,D,C$ in positions $01,10,11$. If $C\subseteq A,D$, both side differences have size at most one, and $C$ uses every remaining coordinate, then isometry forces $A\cap D=C$ and the exact shadow count forces $\operatorname{Sh}(A)\cap\operatorname{Sh}(D)=\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. Hence the paired-square endpoint theorem applies and all parameters are uniquely recovered up to exchanging the two root directions. Within this intrinsic type, rooted minimality is exactly rooted minimality of $(C,0)$ plus the two side endpoint-repair conditions.
proof: The root-fixed $00$ face is connected and contains the root as an isolated vertex, so it is the singleton section. The other sections are uniquely determined. If a word lay in both side sections outside $C$, the opposite side copies would have no intermediate vertex, contradicting isometry; thus their intersection is $C$. All sections and their union are ample. Substituting these facts into the exact four-section shadow formula and using $|\operatorname{Sh}(Z)|=|Z|$ forces the side-shadow intersection to equal $\operatorname{Sh}(C)$. The paired root-transfer criterion then gives recovery and the rooted-minimality equivalence.
